Fundamental — what it's worth: A weighted what-if off the published fair value — not a re-run DCF, and it never touches the Monte Carlo section below. The sizes come from the study’s own sensitivity grids, each of which re-runs the whole unit build, scaled down for the fact that only the cash-flow lenses move. Note which lever dominates: the GROSS MARGIN, not the discount rate. That is the opposite of the previous edition and it follows from the rebuild — terminal value now carries 44.8% of enterprise value rather than 59%, because the terminal return is struck on invested capital at REPLACEMENT cost instead of a 67%-written-down book base. Nudge the margin lever half a point and watch the answer move further than three points of easing does. The margin is also the one driver the study cannot pin down from the filings alone: it has ranged 5.05% to 10.19% across four consecutive filed periods, and it is administered rather than competed.
Technical & price structure: In plain terms: at today’s 21.5% cost of capital the discounted cash flows are worth about EGP 3.8bn while the net debt against them is about EGP 9.8bn — so on the base case the equity is worth nothing, and is floored at zero only because a shareholder cannot owe more than the stake. What EGP 2.19 buys is an option on three things going right together: the receivables collecting, conversion margins recovering from the 1Q26 trough, and the CBE resuming its easing cycle. That’s the bet.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: Our weighted fundamental range is EGP 4.09–8.52 and the widest single lens reaches 9.88 — so the whole simulated price cone sits ABOVE the weighted fair-value range, not around it. Read that gap for what it is: the simulation prices where the tape can travel over three months, the study prices what the business is worth, and the two answer different questions. Nothing in the drift comes from the valuation. The point at which we would rebuild the study is a sustained fundamental move above EGP 9.88 — above the top of every lens — which on the study’s own grids means a permanent gross margin near 12.2%, against a best-ever filed quarter of 10.19%.

One Monte Carlo model, 50,000 paths, driven by the outside forces relevant to a hard-currency industrial exporter listed in a soft-currency market: the LME copper price, the EGP/USD path, the CBE policy corridor and the pace of easing, Egyptian inflation, Gulf and North African grid and infrastructure spending, the order book and its conversion rate, interconnector and data-centre demand for cable and transformers, energy and freight costs, convertibility and repatriation risk on the foreign earnings, and the free float — 11.6% of the shares, with 68% held by the family and 20% by Electra, which is what makes the tape thin.
